clue.text: Mean parents finally going to hospital with sick baby

indicators.note: something sick is out of sorts, so the letters of the following word are put out of order
finally points to the very end of the word before it, so only its closing letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of parents
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
the four letters of baby rearranged

explanation.surface: A mean household where the parents finally take their sick baby to hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby behaviour is unfair or ungenerous, a common sense of mean as in a mean trick.

clue.text: Crusoe cast adrift without source of soap and sugar …

indicators.note: a castaway set adrift is tossed about, so the letters of the name are thrown into disorder
without in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters sit around the single letter

parts.note: the letters of Crusoe rearranged

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of soap

explanation.surface: Robinson Crusoe, adrift with no soap, and the sugar that leads on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Without here means outside, an old sense crosswords love. The ellipsis joins this clue to 2 Down for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucrose is the chemical name for ordinary table sugar, the kind refined from cane and beet.

clue.text: … alert after a wash

parts.note: taken as written
the wash of a boat is the trail of disturbed water it leaves, its wake

explanation.surface: Feeling alert after a wash, the sugar of the previous clue continuing the morning routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Wash sounds like washing yourself, but it is the turbulence behind a moving boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone awake is conscious and paying attention, so the adjective matches alert as in watchful.

clue.text: British capital laid out for plant

indicators.note: laid out suggests spread about, so the word before it has its letters rearranged

parts.note: B is a standard abbreviation for British
the Italian capital city
the letters of laid rearranged

explanation.surface: Planting schemes laid out across the British capital.
explanation.walkthrough: British capital wants to be London, but the capital is a separate one, Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromeliad is a tropical plant of the pineapple family, often grown as a houseplant.

clue.text: 'Momentum' politician visiting Europe wearing scruffy suit

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy and dishevelled, so the following letters come out jumbled
whoever wears something has it around them, so the shuffled letters go round the others

parts.note: the letters of suit rearranged
MP is a Member of Parliament
E is the abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: A politician from the Momentum group turns up in Europe in a scruffy suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Momentum is also the name of a British left-wing campaign group, which is what the quote marks play on.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is driving force that keeps something moving, a close synonym of momentum in physics and ordinary speech.

clue.text: Popular revolutionary is, on reflection, one of us

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the two words before it are read backwards

parts.note: red is a standard word for a communist revolutionary
taken as written

explanation.surface: A popular revolutionary who, thinking it over, turns out to be one of us.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider belongs to the inner group or organisation, so is counted among its own members.

clue.text: Gang of Nazis protected by American author

indicators.note: what is protected is surrounded and shielded, so these letters sit inside the name

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary organisation

explanation.surface: A gang of Nazis sheltered by an American writer, like a wartime thriller plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a group of people, originally one summoned by a sheriff, now any band or crew.

clue.text: Despicable individuals raised money to grow poisonous plant

parts.note: a toad is a contemptible person

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upward, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: Despicable people raising money to cultivate something poisonous.
explanation.walkthrough: Raised looks like fundraising, but it turns loot upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadstool is the everyday name for a poisonous mushroom, loosely treated as a plant.

clue.text: Rose rambling over doctor's grave

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters of the flower stray from their order
lying over something covers it completely, so the shuffled letters enclose the others

parts.note: the letters of rose rearranged
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A rambling rose growing over a doctor's grave in a churchyard.
explanation.walkthrough: Rambling rose is a real kind of climbing rose, so the anagram is well hidden; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and sombre are both adjectives for a serious, gloomy mood or manner.

clue.text: Animal artist with scrapbook in wrong order?

indicators.note: the question mark admits the two parts of the compound word are joined back to front

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
scrap is BIT and book is B; swapped round, book comes first

explanation.surface: An artist who keeps a scrapbook of animal sketches, with the pages jumbled.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrapbook must be split into scrap and book, then the two halves swapped: book comes before scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit is a burrowing mammal with long ears, a plain example of an animal.

clue.text: Rail chaos disturbed cattle

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters of the first two words are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters of rail and chaos rearranged

explanation.surface: Chaos on the railway because cattle have strayed onto the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Charolais is a breed of large white beef cattle that originated in France.

clue.text: Unnatural movement caused by sulphur in processed meat

indicators.note: in places one element inside another, so the element symbol goes within the meat

parts.note: Spam is a brand of tinned processed pork
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A strange twitch brought on by additives in processed meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is an involuntary muscle contraction, a movement the body makes without being willed.

clue.text: Robes expanding to disguise fat

indicators.note: a disguise conceals something within, so the answer lies concealed in the words before

parts.note: found inside these two words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Loose, expanding robes worn to hide a bulging figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese describes a person who is very overweight, an adjective matching fat.

clue.text: Lager and bubbly is brewed outside university

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing and frothing, so the words after it are churned into a new order
outside means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap around the abbreviation

parts.note: the letters of is and brewed rearranged
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Students outside the university brewing lager and fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Bubbly looks like champagne, part of a list of drinks; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Budweiser is a well-known brand of pale lager beer, so the brand is an example of lager.

clue.text: Exclusive European register includes Italian

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: a list that includes something holds it within, so the abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: a register is a list of names
It is short for Italian, as in gin and It (Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: A select European register that admits an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist attitude favours a privileged few and shuts others out, as an exclusive club does.

clue.text: Cook ties cakes to footwear

indicators.note: to cook something is to work it into a different form, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of ties and cakes rearranged

explanation.surface: A baker tying up cakes, with shoes thrown in for no reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice skates are boots fitted with blades for gliding on ice, a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Decorative strip in knitting pattern starts to bulge on needles

parts.note: rib is a knitting stitch pattern of raised ridges

indicators.note: starts are the beginnings of words, so only the opening letter of each following word is used

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A decorative border in a knitting pattern beginning to bulge on the needles.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon is a narrow band of fabric used for trimming and tying, a decorative strip.

clue.text: Mixed dram containing whiskey put into drink that's a comfort at night

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the jumbled letters enclose the radio code letter
put into means inserted, so everything built so far goes inside the drink

parts.note: beer is a drink

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters of the short word are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of dram rearranged
Whiskey is the NATO alphabet word for W

explanation.surface: A cocktail of whisky and other drinks, the nightcap that comforts you at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Whiskey and dram look like real drinks, but whiskey is just the radio code word for the letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed warmer, such as a pan of hot coals or a hot-water bottle, heats the sheets for comfort when sleeping.

clue.text: Criminal losing old female guard

indicators.note: losing means letting something go, so the two abbreviations are taken away from the word

parts.note: a criminal is an offender
O is the abbreviation for old
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A criminal who has lost an old lady, guarded by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fender is a protective barrier, such as a fireguard or a buffer on a boat, so it guards.

clue.text: A Liberal in government put straight again

indicators.note: in places the first two items inside the word for rule

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal in government putting things right once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to bring back into line, which is restoring straightness a second time.

clue.text: Busybody cleric left in lake

indicators.note: in places the letters for the churchman and the direction inside the water

parts.note: meer is a variant spelling of mere, a lake
DD is a Doctor of Divinity, a cleric
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A nosy cleric left stranded in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling of a lake is mere, but the less common variant meer is needed for the letters to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddler interferes in other people's affairs, which is what a busybody does.

clue.text: Make a mistake with popular bun for toasting

parts.note: to muff is to bungle
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Getting the order wrong at a bakery with a well-liked bun.
explanation.definitionFit: An English muffin is a flat yeast bread roll usually split and toasted before eating.

clue.text: Militant is awful cad and liar

indicators.note: awful means dreadfully bad, so the letters that follow are mangled into a new order

parts.note: the letters of cad and liar rearranged, leaving out the and

explanation.surface: A militant described as a terrible cad and a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: The word and joins the two words of fodder and contributes no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical holds extreme views and pushes for sweeping change, close to militant.

clue.text: Each dish wrapped by expert

indicators.note: something wrapped by another is enclosed in it, so the food goes inside

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a pie is a dish

explanation.surface: Every dish wrapped up by a master chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for each one, as in they cost a pound apiece.

clue.text: Man after fish with handle of weapon

indicators.note: after fixes the order, putting the word for crewing behind the fish

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A fisherman going after fish, carrying a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Man reads as a noun, a person, but it is the verb meaning to crew or staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikestaff is the long wooden shaft of a pike, the old infantry spear, so the weapon's handle.

clue.text: Little American leaving animals standing

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up reads from bottom to top, so the result is turned around
leaving means departing, so the abbreviation is taken out of the word

parts.note: llamas are South American animals
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A small American walking away from animals that are standing still.
explanation.definitionFit: Small and little are both everyday adjectives for something of limited size.

clue.text: Hospital leaving injured protected?

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so the abbreviation departs from the word

parts.note: injured means harmed
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: An injured patient discharged from hospital, perhaps under guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the definition is loose: being armed is a way of protecting yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone armed carries weapons for defence, so is in a sense protected.

clue.text: Child carrying king's headgear

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so the abbreviation sits inside the word for youngster

parts.note: a mite is a small child
R is Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A child carrying the king's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: King's looks possessive, but the 's stands for is, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed headdress worn by bishops, a kind of headgear.

clue.text: Actor in next Rambo?

indicators.note: in says the answer is lodged within the words that follow

parts.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: Casting someone in the next Rambo film.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that a minor bit-part player in the next Rambo sequel fits the whole clue too.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a film performer in a crowd scene with no lines, a minor actor.

clue.text: Graduate in absurd situation using language like a native

indicators.note: in places the degree inside the word for foolish

parts.note: an absurd situation is an idiotic one
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate abroad, stuck in a ridiculous predicament, managing in the local tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic speech uses the natural expressions and turns of phrase that fluent native speakers use.

clue.text: Foreign character records dancing lion

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of the big cat swap places

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
the letters of lion rearranged

explanation.surface: A foreign performer who records a dancing lion act.
explanation.walkthrough: Foreign character looks like a person from abroad, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: Gold found by source of river

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Gold discovered at the source of a river, like a prospector's lucky strike.
explanation.walkthrough: Source of river reads as one phrase, but river alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orwell is a river in Suffolk, in eastern England, flowing to the sea at Felixstowe.
